content_metadata.description: An in-depth analysis of the visual effects breakdown video for the film 'The Impossible', highlighting the challenges and innovative techniques used to realistically depict a tsunami.

qAndA.answer: The backdrop used for the miniature model set is green.
qAndA.question: What color is the backdrop used in the miniature model set?

qAndA.answer: The filmmakers had only one take to destroy the miniature model.
qAndA.question: How many takes did the filmmakers have to destroy the miniature model of the resort?

qAndA.answer: The filmmakers used real-life footage of unsuccessful test waves that were naturally dirty to create the look of the tsunami wave.
qAndA.question: What was used to make the wave look 'dirty'?

qAndA.answer: The filmmakers decided to use real water for authenticity and a more visceral impact, despite financial limitations and technical challenges.
qAndA.question: Why did the filmmakers choose to use real water instead of CGI for the tsunami?

qAndA.answer: Fear was the most prominent emotion experienced by the actors, particularly Tom Holland, due to the intensity and realism of the wave simulation.
qAndA.question: What emotion was most prominently evoked in the actors during the filming of the wave sequence?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: You don't know what cannot be done and then you're there to do certain things that wouldn't have been done otherwise.
I think what we got on the screen is great.
If you really want to make it true to what happened, you need to recreate a tsunami in a very realistic way.
In a story like this, it was very important to be as truthful as we possibly could.
We didn't really know how we were going to do it.
Being a film based upon a real story, we came to the conclusion that we couldn't use digital water.
People kept telling us, oh no, you cannot do the wave with real water. It has to be CGI.
And we didn't have the money for that.
We started to investigate how to mix real layers of water that could recreate that feeling of an ocean.
The wave that you have for a tsunami is a very different shape from a regular sea wave that we normally make.
When the team decided they wanted to have a really dirty wave, we weren't sure that we could actually make such a thing.
So we started looking through all of our tapes and we found the worst waves that we could ever make.
One's where the test had all gone wrong and so it started really bad.
The Orchid Beach Resort is Brandon, we just opened a week ago. You love it here.
We built a 13 scale model of the Orchid Beach Resort pool and the whole area of bungalows.
And we only had one chance, one only take to destroy that model.
So we had to set up all the frames at once and each frame requires specific camera.
And I think there was a moment that we lost track of how many cameras we had inside that model for only one take.
We had many discussions about what the wave would do when it hit particular panels, what we could blow through, what damaging we'd do.
And so this is where the skill of the Magicon team came in because they had to make something that would break up in a realistic way.
There was a decisive moment which was the moment we had to push that button.
Ah, come on!
It was one of those things where the acting was really required because at times I was genuinely scared.
I'm not 25, I'm not Tom's age and it's not normal for me to be thrust around like this.
It was a hard thing to do.
We're learning as we went along.
